excerpt: TestSprite is an AI agent that writes, runs and repairs end-to-end tests for web apps and APIs. Free plan; paid from $19/month. Version 3.0 and alternatives.
content:
TestSprite is an AI testing agent for software teams. You point it at a running web app or API, optionally with a product spec, and it explores the app, writes end-to-end tests, runs them in a real browser or against the live API, and reports what broke. Each failure comes with the failing step, screenshots, a DOM snapshot, the test source, a guess at the root cause and a suggested fix. Passing tests are kept, so the suite grows over time, and tests repair themselves when the interface changes.

It works through a no-code web dashboard, an MCP server inside editors such as Cursor and VS Code, an open-source command-line tool (Apache 2.0) that coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor can call, and a GitHub check that re-tests each pull request. Version 3.0, dated 24 April 2026 in the changelog, added a parallel fleet of agents that explore the app before tests are written, a rebuilt backend testing engine, a feature map extracted from an uploaded spec, and reusable test files and fixtures.

TestSprite gives its address as Seattle, Washington, and has a free plan, with paid plans from $19 a month. The company says more than 100,000 developers use it; that is its own figure.

TestSprite launched on Product Hunt on 22 May 2026 and finished #1 for the day, with 465 upvotes and 66 comments. It has 4 Product Hunt reviews averaging 4.75 out of 5 (as of 14 October 2026).

We have not tested TestSprite ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing page, changelog and CLI page, its Product Hunt listing and the official pricing pages of comparable tools, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.platform: Web app, MCP server, CLI and GitHub integration
profile.summary_short: AI agent that writes, runs and repairs end-to-end tests for web apps and APIs
use_cases: Getting a first end-to-end test suite for an app that has none
Letting a coding agent check its own changes before you merge them
Running nightly or per-release regression tests on a schedule
Testing backend APIs, including flows that depend on several calls

fit: build with AI coding agents and want the changes checked end to end
have little or no test coverage and no time to write Playwright or Cypress scripts
want test results posted on pull requests
not_fit: need to keep testing fully in-house without a hosted service: the CLI needs a TestSprite account and API key
want fixed, predictable costs: plans are measured in monthly credits
test native mobile apps: the site talks about browsers and APIs only

pricing.intro: TestSprite's own pricing page, in US dollars, monthly prices. The page has a yearly toggle saying "Save 35%" but we did not see yearly prices.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 150 credits a month, 1 environment, 1 test list, 30 days of run history, pull-request testing on 1 GitHub repo

plans.name: Starter
plans.detail: 400 credits, auto-healing tests, advanced backend testing, 10 scheduled runs, 3 GitHub repos

plans.name: Standard
plans.detail: 800 credits, 3 environments, Jira and Linear integrations, a more advanced agent model, 5 GitHub repos

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: 1,600 credits, unlimited environments and run history, unlimited pull-request testing, the most capable agent model

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.price: From $199/month (10 seats or more), contact sales
plans.detail: From 5,000 credits, single-tenant deployment, SSO/SCIM and audit logs, a named success manager

notes: The pricing page does not mention refunds.
The company says it is SOC 2 certified.

alternatives.intro: Two AI testing services and one widely used open-source framework. Prices come from each product's own pages, checked on 14 October 2026.

items.name: QA.tech
items.what: AI agent that runs manual-style test journeys from plain-language goals
items.difference: Similar agent-led approach, but every plan is priced on request and there is no listed free plan.

items.name: Momentic
items.what: AI test automation for browser and mobile apps written as plain-English steps
items.difference: You describe test steps yourself rather than letting an agent explore and write the suite; it also covers mobile apps.

items.name: Playwright
items.what: Open-source browser automation and testing framework from Microsoft
items.difference: No AI agent or hosted service: you write and maintain the test code yourself, at no licence cost.

pros: Free plan that includes the full test loop and pull-request testing on one repo
Works from a dashboard, an editor via MCP, a terminal or CI
Failure reports include screenshots, a DOM snapshot, a root-cause guess and a suggested fix
Tests repair themselves when the interface changes
cons: Usage is metered in credits, so heavy use needs a higher plan
Needs a TestSprite account even for the open-source CLI
No refund policy shown on the pricing page
Headline numbers (users, accuracy gains) are the company's own

posts.author: Piyush Garg
posts.note: recommends TestSprite as an AI-powered testing tool

posts.author: Trae
posts.note: the AI code editor's account praises the TestSprite MCP server

faq.a: An AI testing agent that explores a running web app or API, writes end-to-end tests, runs them and reports failures with a suggested fix. It can be used from a web dashboard, an editor via MCP, a CLI or GitHub pull requests.
There is a free plan with 150 credits a month and one GitHub repo. Paid plans are $19, $39 and $69 a month, and Enterprise starts at $199 a month for 10 seats or more.

According to the changelog: a parallel fleet of agents explores the live app before tests are written, the backend testing engine was rebuilt, an editable feature map can be extracted from an uploaded spec, and reusable files and fixtures can be wired into tests.

faq.q: Does it work with Claude Code, Codex or Cursor?
faq.a: Yes. The CLI page lists Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline and Antigravity, and the MCP server runs inside editors. The CLI needs Node.js 20 or newer and a TestSprite API key.
Yes. TestSprite says the CLI is released under the Apache 2.0 licence, with its source on GitHub.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to TestSprite?
faq.a: QA.tech and Momentic are AI testing services; Playwright is a free open-source framework where you write the tests yourself.
